newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italian parliamentary commission rejects mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italian parliamentary commission rejects mini-budget.

text.p: The budget commission of Italy's lower house of parliament voted on Friday against the government's proposed 1997 mini-budget after two centre-left deputies broke ranks, officials said.

The supplementary budget aims to reduce the 1997 budget deficit by 15.5 trillion lire ($9.1 billion) in the hope of keeping Italy on track to meet the deficit target needed to join Europe's planned single currency.
The mini-budget will now go to the full Chamber of Deputies for a vote but the result was seen as an embarrassment for Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government.
The measure failed to pass by just one vote, with 25 members weighing in against and 24 in favour, the commission's office said.

The vote was essentially a challenge to the government to put the mini-budget to a confidence test in the full chamber, said Mauro Paissan, a senior member of the Greens party which is part of Prodi's centre-left coalition.
"Basically, what the (government) majority and the opposition have done is to ask the government to call a confidence vote," he told reporters.
The two supporters of the Olive Tree coalition who voted against the measure were former members of Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's Italian Renewal group in parliament.
The hard-left Communist Refoundation, key government allies who hold the balance of power in the lower house, voted with the government.

Roberto Villetti, of a small socialist party also part of Prodi's Olive Tree coalition, voted against the package in the committee but told reporters afterwards he would vote for the government in the case of a confidence vote.
"We don't want to be part of an unstable government, therefore if the government has to call a confidence vote on this question, we will vote for it," he said.

Italian financial markets before the vote were already recording losses amid concerns that Italy would miss the deficit target. But they dipped further on the news before recovering to pre-vote levels.

The lira was quoted close to the day's lows at 988 per mark by 1345 GMT, the key government bond futures contract on LIFFE fell half a point before recovering and the blue-chip Mib30 share index was around 0.3 percent lower.
The budget commission has approved individual amendments to the measures but without final approval for the whole package it passes to the full chamber in its original form.
There the individual amendments must be re-examined from scratch, said commission chairman Bruno Solaroli.
Some measures in the package have been severely criticised by the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance and industry.
Businesses in particular have complained about one section that aims to raise 1997 revenue by bringing forward tax payments due on companies' pools of severance payment funds.
The additional budget, unveiled in March, is crucial to Prodi's bid to win Italy a place among the founding members of European monetary union due to start in 1999.
One of the qualifying criteria stipulates that the budget deficit must not exceed three percent of gross domestic product or economic output.

The government maintains the extra measures are enough to reach that goal by the deadline at the end of this year although EU Commission officials have forecast that Italy will miss the threshold by 0.2 of a percentage point.
